_comment: PLAT-35 — THE TIER-4 READINGS OF THE GPUI FRONT-END'S OWN FRAMES.
WHY THIS IS A SEPARATE FILE FROM `tier4-review.json`, SAID FIRST BECAUSE
THE SPLIT IS THE DECISION MOST LIKELY TO BE READ AS EVASION.
`tier4-review.json` is the gated deliverable: the suite refuses it four
ways and a reading scoring below 4 BLOCKS unless it is in that file's
`knownRed` block, which asserts in both directions that the quarantined
set is EXACTLY the set scoring below 4. Every reading below scores 3 or 4.
Putting them there would mean quarantining ten of twelve, and a quarantine
ledger holding ten of twelve entries is not a quarantine — it is the gate
switched off while wearing the shape of a gate. So the SCORES here are
ungated, the findings are carried in PLAT-35's status with
owners, and `tier4-review.json` is left exactly as it was: six readings of
the ELECTRON arm, with its two quarantines.
THE SCORES ARE UNGATED. THE FILE IS NOT (added 2026-10-02).
`src/frontend/gpui/tests/test_plat35_ledger_integrity.nim` re-derives this
file's `gate` counts from its own `findings`, checks `gate.met` against
them in BOTH directions, requires a unique id, an owner, a closed-set
severity and substantial text on every finding, refuses a finding that is
both resolved and unresolved, and checks the reading population against
`scenarios.json` — count per iteration, each scenario once, and every
reading's view and viewport against that file's own tables. Until that
suite existed NOTHING in the tree read this file: `grep -rn` for its name
found it in prose only. An unread ledger's least reliable sentence is its
own summary, which is `Verification-Harness-Traps.md` 4; declining to gate
a SCORE is a decision, and leaving a record unread is not one.
WHAT THESE READINGS ARE OF. The first frames of the GPUI front-end's own
scene ever captured on any host. Before them PLAT-35's GPUI arm was the
SHADOW TREE only (`PLAT35-VG1`), so no tier-4 reading of that front-end
existed to score. `ci/test/plat35-gpui-capture.sh` produced them through
`codetracer-gpui --pixels-out`.
THEY ARE AGENT READINGS, DECLARED AS SUCH, exactly as `tier4-review.json`
declares its six. There have been ZERO human reviews of the GPUI arm.
HOW TO READ THE RATINGS. The brief's own grammar makes below-4 a MISSING
OR DISTORTED ELEMENT rather than an aesthetic opinion, and every reading
below is there for the same first finding: the GPUI window draws no
debug-controls strip at all, in any scenario, where the expected-elements
block requires the nine transport buttons. That is one defect reported six
times, not six defects.
THE GATE IS THE LEDGER AND NOT THE NUMBER. `findings` below is the
ledger; PLAT-35's status carries it with an owner per entry. Seven P1 and
six P2 entries are unresolved, so the gate is NOT met and the milestone
stays `partial`.
subject: codetracer-gpui

What was NOT re-measured is the only thing that matters for the
readings themselves: what the six scenarios now look like.
findingsThisMayHAVERESOLVED: PLAT35-F1 (`no debug-controls strip anywhere: none of the nine
transport buttons is drawn in any scenario`) is the clearest candidate:
`TransportControls` ARE the nine buttons, and `main.drawTopBar` paints
them into every window this front-end opens. **IT IS LEFT UNRESOLVED
AND COUNTED ANYWAY**, which is the point of saying so here: moving a
finding to `resolved` needs a `confirmedBy` reading, and there is no
reading. Counting it resolved on the strength of reading the upstream
diff would be exactly the blind assertion this ledger is graded
against. The same caution applies to any finding about the tab strip or
the pane chrome, which `96c78119f` also moved.
WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: one run of `just plat35-capture-gpui` on a host
with a `calc` recording, then iteration 3 in this file.

note: were taken against. This host's only `calc` recording is a 10-line
program, so `returned-calltrace` cannot reach `main`/`evaluate` at line
110 and every frame shows ten source rows. Filed as PLAT35-C1 below:
it is a CAPTURE-PROVENANCE fact and it is stated here rather than left
for a reviewer to report as a product defect — one of the six
iteration-1 readings did exactly that, which is the cost of not stating

iterations.changed: the declared monospace face is APPLIED to the editor's code, its gutter and its inline values (chrome.MonoFontFamily + main.applyTextFaces). Nothing else — no layout, no palette, no new pane, no glyph.
firstAttemptFailed: The first version of this fix set one family name for both platforms
and RE-CAPTURED SIX BYTE-IDENTICAL FRAMES. `MacTextSystem` resolves a
family through Core Text, which never reads the dev shell's
`Courier.ttc`, `Menlo.ttc`, `SFNSMono.ttf` and no DejaVu — so the name
resolved to nothing and the text system fell back to what it had been
drawing. The per-platform split is the repair, and the byte-identical
re-capture is the measurement that found it.

readings.evidence: the gutter digits 1-9 now share one right-aligned column with 10 and the pointer sits in its own lane, so the active row's number no longer shifts; every top-level token starts at the identical x and the 4- and 8-space indents step in exact monospace multiples
code and gutter genuinely monospace with uniform advance and a stable code left edge; the state pane's values are still proportional, which is PLAT35-VG8's scope rather than this fix's
monospace landed on code, gutter and the inline value row; the clipping at 1440 is unchanged, which the fix never claimed to address
indentation lines up character-for-character and 1-10 share a fixed digit width where iteration 1 showed proportional glyphs
the editor's code, gutter and the inline chip are monospace with stable advance; the event-log table itself is still proportional (PLAT35-VG8)
the right edges of 1, 2, 6 and 10 all land on the same x, so neither the breakpoint dot nor the pointer displaces its digit any more

resolved.finding: the editor's code and gutter were set in a proportional sans, so glyph advances varied and code columns did not line up
resolved.remedy: chrome.MonoFontFamily, applied by main.applyTextFaces from each element's DECLARED text metric

resolved.finding: the gutter's pointer and mark lanes displaced the line number, so numbers 2/6/10 each sat at a different x and top-level defs appeared mis-indented
resolved.remedy: the same one — the lanes are one GLYPH wide each, which is a fixed-width column in a monospaced face and in no other
resolved.confirmedBy: the shell and editorWithMark iteration-2 readings, each quoting the x-alignment directly

findings.finding: no debug-controls strip anywhere: none of the nine transport buttons is drawn in any scenario. The window's top edge goes straight into the pane row.
findings.measurement: 6 of 6 readings in both iterations report it as their first finding; it is why every score is at or below 4.
findings.cause: layout_model.sharedDefaultLayout() carries no debugControls pane — the desktop draws them as a toolbar rather than as a pane — so there is no slot for a GPUI leaf to render them into.
findings.owner: PLAT-21 (the milestone that built the debugger surfaces) / PLAT-40

findings.finding: the call-trace pane lists frames and marks none as current — no highlight, caret or weight difference.
findings.measurement: the brief's `editor` block requires 'the call-trace pane lists frames, with one marked as current'; `main #2` is weighted exactly like `add #3`..`add #7`.

findings.finding: the editor clips a source line mid-token at the pane's right edge with no ellipsis, no wrap and no horizontal scrollbar, so the rest of the statement is unrecoverable.
findings.measurement: line 7 reads `total = add(total` and stops. `renderEditorRow` sets `white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden` on the code span and `text-overflow: ellipsis` on the inline VALUE only — the code deliberately never elides, which was the right call at a wide viewport and loses information at a narrow one.
findings.owner: PLAT-35 — and it is the GPUI twin of PLAT35-PD1, which is the same defect in the Electron panes. Deciding whether the answer is an ellipsis or a scrollbar is one decision for both front-ends.

findings.finding: the state pane's rows are flat `name: value` strings: no type field, and no column structure, so name, type and value cannot be distinguished and nothing aligns vertically.
findings.measurement: the brief's `editor` block requires 'name, type and value per row'.

findings.finding: the event-log pane shows no row count in its footer.
findings.measurement: the brief's `eventLog` block requires 'a visible row count in its footer'. The columns and the headers ARE present — which corrects PLAT-37's forward-attributed reading that GPUI's Event Log is 'a vertical stack of cells … no column layout at all'; measured 2026-10-02, it is a table with aligned `#` / `kind` / `value` columns.

findings.finding: the Files pane reports 'no source files have been loaded for this recording' while the editor beside it renders that recording's source. Two panes of one window contradict each other about one fact.
findings.measurement: 6 of 6 readings in both iterations; two of them graded it P1 unprompted ('one of the two is lying').
findings.cause: native_host.recordingFileTree reads `<traceFolder>/paths.json` and returns an empty tree when there is none. A CTFS bundle keeps its paths INSIDE the container (`paths.dat` / `paths.off`, present in this recording's root directory), so the pane is starved on every `.ct` recording while the editor reads the same sources through the store.

findings.finding: the state pane elides `__file__`'s value mid-path, so the filename is unrecoverable at 1440x900.
findings.measurement: distinct from F3: this one IS elided with an ellipsis rather than amputated, so the defect is that there is no way to reach the rest, not that the user cannot tell it was cut.

findings.finding: the source editor occupies about 24% of the window's width, not the brief's 'left three-quarters', and is not leftmost; the Files pane sits left of it and the event-log pane takes more width than the editor.
findings.measurement: editor x≈395..865 of 1920 at the wide viewport.
findings.owner: PLAT-45 — the arrangement comes from `layout_model.sharedDefaultLayout()`, which the terminal and the desktop also open, so it is NOT a GPUI-only change and must not be made as one.

findings.finding: every pane names itself twice — a tab label immediately above a heading repeating the same word — and the state pane says 'State' three times (tab, heading, first row) while Locals/Globals/Watches render as plain stacked rows rather than a tab strip.
findings.measurement: 6 of 6 readings. The duplication is PLAT-47's tab strips landing on top of a heading that predates them; the heading is load-bearing for PLAT-20's plan-order text assertions ('keeping it as the first child means the arrangement assertions still have something to read'), so removing it is not a one-line change.

findings.finding: the editor pane's background reads as a different surface from every other pane — 'two palettes in one window'.
findings.measurement: the editor uses `leaves.EditorGround` (a design token) and every other pane uses `chrome.chromeOf(crPaneBackground)`, which `chrome.nim`'s own header states was CHOSEN in PLAT-37 and is not read from `codetracer-design-system`, 'because that repository publishes no hex for any member of layout_questions.DesignTokenAlphabet'. So the split is between a token and a placeholder, and the module already says where the fix lands.
findings.owner: PLAT-35 / the first Electron-GUI milestone (the design-system mapping)

findings.finding: the inline value is drawn as a C comment — `/* total: 10 */` — inside Python source, where the Electron reference draws a chip.
findings.measurement: Electron's `.flow-inline-value-box` (src/frontend/styles/components/flow.styl) is `border-radius: 2px`, `font-family: monospace`, `text-overflow: ellipsis`, on `colors-editor-surface-primary`, with NO delimiters. `leaves.inlineValueText` wraps the pairs in `/* … */`.
findings.blockedBy: NOT FIXED IN THIS PASS, with the reason measured rather than asserted: `src/frontend/gpui/tests/plat42_gutter.nim`'s `valueCommentName` and `test_plat42_window.nim` both PARSE that spelling out of OCR ('A value comment is `/* name…`, not any `/*`'), and PLAT-42's window lane is Wayland-only, so the re-grade that a spelling change requires cannot be run on this host. A fix that reddens another milestone's lane in a commit that cannot run it is worse than a stated finding.
findings.owner: PLAT-35, jointly with PLAT-42's OCR grammar

findings.finding: the event-log table has no header rule, no column dividers and no zebra, and its header row is the same weight and colour as a data row, so the header does not read as a header.

the breakpoint glyph is the same dim grey as the line-number digits and about 4px across, so it reads as a bullet rather than as a breakpoint, and it abuts its digit while the execution pointer has clear separation — one lane, two different paddings.
findings.measurement: the x-position half of this finding WAS fixed this pass (see PLAT35-F16); the colour and size half is unchanged. `leaves.BreakpointGlyph` is `●` and takes the gutter span's colour, which is the line-number colour.

findings.finding: the MARK has no reserved lane in the gutter. The breakpoint dot occupies the mono cell immediately LEFT of the ones digit, and that is the same cell the TENS digit occupies on a line number >= 10 — so the dot forms no column a reader (or PLAT-39's ink-cluster reader) can scan down, and on a two-digit row it shifts left into the execution pointer's cell instead.
findings.measurement: DERIVED FROM THE CODE AND THEN CONFIRMED IN THE PIXELS, 2026-10-02. `leaves.gutterText` is `<padding><pointer><mark><number><gap>` right-aligned as ONE run with the padding IN FRONT of the lanes, so at numberWidth=2 a one-digit row lays out [sp][sp][dot][2] and a two-digit row lays out [sp][sp][1][0]: the mark and the tens digit are both at cell index 2. Confirmed by decoding `build/plat35/gpui/editorWithMark.png` and taking per-row ink intervals over the gutter strip (editor pane left edge x=302; line-number ones cell x 342-350; GutterGap x 351-390; code from x 391). Only the three rows with gutter content ink at all: line 2 at x 331-341 (grey 87 — the dot), line 6 at x 322-332 (grey 200 — the execution pointer, one cell further left because the mark cell is empty) and line 10 at x 333-341 (grey 84 — the tens digit). The dot lane and the tens-digit lane are one 9.75px cell, x 332-341.
findings.notExercised: PLAT35-C1's 10-line recording has exactly ONE two-digit row, and `breakpoint-editor` puts its mark on a one-digit row, so no captured frame shows a mark and a tens digit in that lane at the same time. The corpus cannot fail this; only the arithmetic shows it.
findings.cause: the padding precedes the lanes rather than separating them from the number. That is deliberate — `gutterText`'s own comment says it is so that `GutterGap` stays the only wide gap on a row, which is what PLAT-39's reader locates the gutter's end by — and this is its consequence. A fix reserves one cell per lane and pads between the lanes and the number, which moves every gutter x in every frame, so it is a capture-and-re-grade change rather than a one-line one.
findings.owner: PLAT-35 (the geometry is `leaves.gutterText`, the row shared with PLAT-3) — jointly PLAT35-C1, because it cannot be closed from a 10-line corpus

findings.finding: CONFIRMED FROM PIXELS, having been a structural claim until now: the state, call-trace and event-log panes render in the window's proportional face because PLAT-3's medium-independent tree carries no text role and therefore no metric, so the window's face walk has nothing to act on there.
findings.measurement: 'every value in the State pane still renders proportional'; 'the event-log table is still proportional'. Asserted in `test_plat35_text_faces.nim`, which measures the gap's SCOPE (zero metric-carrying elements in a pane-view subtree, against a non-zero count in the editor's) rather than quoting it.

findings.finding: this host's `calc` recording is a 10-line program, not the 116-line `test-programs/calc/main.py` the brief's per-view measurements were taken against.
findings.consequence: `returned-calltrace` cannot reach `main`/`evaluate` at line 110, so the brief's clause about the caller's frame being current is not exercised; every frame shows ten source rows, so the density findings are read against a shorter file than the corpus intends.
findings.cause: the fixture provider records `calc` through `codetracer-python-recorder`, which this workspace cannot provision (`test-logs/tui-fixtures/` does not exist here).

gate.rule: zero unresolved P1 and P2 findings
gate.note: A numeric rating is a summary of this ledger and not a substitute for it. The two iterations moved two views from 3 to 4 and resolved two P2 entries; FIFTEEN remain — seven P1 and eight P2 — and six of the seven P1 entries are owned by PLAT-21, PLAT-40 or PLAT-41 rather than by PLAT-35. These three numbers are no longer only prose: `src/frontend/gpui/tests/test_plat35_ledger_integrity.nim` RE-DERIVES unresolvedP1 and unresolvedP2 from `findings` and checks `met` against them in both directions, so a count that drifts from its own ledger is a failing case rather than a sentence nobody reads. PLAT35-F14 was added 2026-10-02 by a review of this pass, from the captured pixels and the gutter arithmetic, AFTER the two iterations were recorded; the readings are deliberately NOT re-scored for it, because a reading is what an agent said on a date.
